finding.metric: Q3 2026 year-over-year non-GAAP core revenue/sales growth
finding.precision: Both 10-Q and Exhibit 99.1 print 3.0% (one decimal); no more precise Q3 value found in these official documents.
finding.quarter: Three months ended 2026-09-25 vs comparable 2025 period
finding.scope: 10-Q says core sales excludes acquired/divested business effects, currency translation, and—beginning with this report—tariff refunds to customers. Respiratory testing is separately excluded only in the separately labeled 5.5% measure. The market criterion’s “core revenue growth” maps to the reported 3.0% total-company measure, not GAAP revenue growth (8.5%), 5.5% excluding respiratory testing, or Q4 forward guidance (~3.0%).
finding.source_comparison: The filed 10-Q narrative and table state 3.0%; Exhibit 99.1 repeats the same total-company 3.0% and tariff note. The company IR release previously captured also stated 3.0%. No alternate Q3 definition/value found across these captured materials. Frozen rule directs use of most numerically precise version and excludes definition/scope variants; here sources agree at 0.1 percentage point.
finding.tariff_context: Refunds relate to tariffs collected by Danaher in prior periods and returned or expected to be returned to customers. In Q3 these refunds decreased reported sales 1.0%; the reconciliation lists tariff refunds +1.0% as a bridge component, acquisitions/divestitures -6.5%, currency ~0, GAAP sales growth 8.5%, and reported non-GAAP core growth 3.0%. Thus the separately listed refund line is consistent with the 3.0% core measure after adjusting reported sales for customer refunds; it does not establish a different/more precise Q3 core figure. 10-Q says IEEPA refund impact on net earnings, net of refunds to customers, was < $100m.
